terms: Forum sur la gouvernance de l'internet

sub_indicators.label: Consultation on digital law and policy
sub_indicators.subject: gov.discourse
sub_indicators.text: Non-governmental contribution to national policy: consultation on digital law and policy
sub_indicators.norm_short: The African Charter on Democracy, Elections and Governance commits its parties to dialogue between government, civil society and the private sector. The Malabo Convention, Article 24, asks each party to draw up its cybersecurity policy with stakeholders. Neither says how.
criteria: A source from the past three years says a named digital law or policy was made without consulting people outside government, or that they were refused a part in it, and none says they were asked.

In the past three years the government, parliament or a regulator asked people outside government for their views on a named digital law or policy: a draft put out for comment, or a hearing, workshop or meeting they took part in. A national internet governance forum, a consultation on something that is not digital, and a workshop of officials, donors and consultants do not count.
In the past three years it published what it was told: a report of the consultation, the comments received, or its written answer to them.

In the past three years a consultation on a digital law or policy was held because a law, decree or published procedure required it. The rule alone, with no consultation held under it, does not count.
In the past three years a standing body with members from outside government gave its view on a named digital law or policy. A body that has only been set up or has only met does not count.

aspects.name: Consultation and what was published of it
